settings.heading: Overview
settings.body:
SemiProbe designs and manufactures a family of non-thermal chucks from 50 mm to 300 mm, used on our probe systems and on other probe systems — home built or competitive. In most cases the device under test — die, partial wafer, whole wafer, substrate, PCB or packaged part — is held in place with vacuum using a round chuck with concentric vacuum rings.

The chucks can be biased, grounded or floating. We also manufacture high frequency chucks with vacuum holes and two calibration substrate holders (auxiliary chucks). All chucks have independent vacuum control. The standard chuck plating is electroless nickel, but other plating materials are available on request.

settings.heading: Choosing a Configuration
settings.bar_text: Probing at high frequency, or need a plating material we do not list?

settings.title: START WITH THE WAFER SIZE
settings.description: Chuck diameter should match the largest substrate you handle. Standard chucks run from 50 mm through 300 mm; the high frequency range starts at 100 mm. A larger chuck will hold smaller substrates, so size for your biggest device under test.

settings.title: STANDARD OR HIGH FREQUENCY
settings.description: Standard chucks use concentric vacuum rings and suit DC, analytical and production probing. High frequency chucks use vacuum holes and include two calibration substrate holders, which is what RF, microwave and millimetre-wave measurement needs.

settings.title: DECIDE HOW THE CHUCK SITS ELECTRICALLY
settings.description: Every chuck can be biased, grounded or floating, and each has independent vacuum control. Tell us how the chuck needs to sit relative to your measurement and we will confirm the right configuration before you order.

settings.question: Will these chucks fit a non-SemiProbe probe system?
settings.answer: In most cases, yes. The chucks are used on our probe systems and on other probe systems, home built or competitive. Send us your stage details and we will confirm fit before you order.

settings.question: What is the difference between a standard and a high frequency chuck?
settings.answer: Standard chucks hold the device with concentric vacuum rings. High frequency chucks use vacuum holes and include two calibration substrate holders (auxiliary chucks), which is what RF and millimetre-wave calibration requires.

settings.question: Can the chuck be biased or grounded?
settings.answer: Yes. The chucks can be biased, grounded or floating, and each has independent vacuum control.

settings.question: Do you offer other plating materials?
settings.answer: The standard plating is electroless nickel. Other plating materials are available — contact us with your requirement and we will quote it.

settings.question: Do I need a vacuum pump?
settings.answer: The chuck needs a vacuum supply. If your station does not have house vacuum, our small-footprint vacuum pumps are sized for wafer chucks and manipulators.

settings.heading: Need a Chuck We Don't List?
settings.body: SemiProbe manufactures wafer chucks to order — alternative plating materials, non-standard diameters, thermal variants and auxiliary chucks for proprietary test environments.
